edits.old:
Pullback preserves the curvature inequality, and a genuine potential stays genuine because $\pi$ is surjective. Conversely, restrict a $\theta$-plurisubharmonic function $u$ to an elliptic fiber. Locally a smooth potential for $\theta_B$ makes $u$ plurisubharmonic after pullback correction. The restriction is therefore subharmonic or identically $-\infty$. Since the correction is constant along the fiber, $u$ itself is subharmonic there. Compactness and connectedness imply that it is constant, allowing the value $-\infty$.

Thus $u=v\circ\pi$ for a function $v$ on $B$. On each base coordinate patch a holomorphic section identifies $v$ with the restriction of $u$ to that section. The corrected restriction is plurisubharmonic and cannot be identically $-\infty$ on an open patch: that would make $u$ identically $-\infty$ on an open subset of $X$. Hence $v$ is a genuine $\theta_B$-plurisubharmonic function. Surjectivity of $\pi$ gives uniqueness and preservation of ordinary order, with exactly the same constants.
edits.new: The form $\theta_B$ is closed, and $\pi$ is a proper holomorphic submersion with connected fibers. Thus \cref{prop:psh-descent-submersion} gives the asserted bijection. Surjectivity of $\pi$ also shows that an ordinary singularity inequality holds upstairs exactly when it holds downstairs, with the same constant.

edits.old: A local frame of $L_B^m$ pulls back to a frame on $\pi^{-1}(U)$. The coefficient of a holomorphic section on this set is constant on each compact connected elliptic fiber, by the maximum principle. Local holomorphic sections of $\pi$ show that this coefficient descends holomorphically. These descended sections patch uniquely. Membership in the selecting ideals descends as well, by the ideal identity and reflection of membership proved above. This proves the isomorphism. For $v=0$, the usual bihomogeneous polynomial basis on $\mathbf P^1\times\mathbf P^1$ has $(am+1)(bm+1)$ elements.
edits.new: The selected-space identification is \cref{prop:partial-kernel-submersion}, applied to $L_B$ and $v$ on the base. For $v=0$, the usual bihomogeneous polynomial basis on $\mathbf P^1\times\mathbf P^1$ has $(am+1)(bm+1)$ elements.

edits.old: For a competitor $a$, consider $b=\max(a-C,q)$. It is $\theta$-plurisubharmonic and below zero. The valuative order criterion of \cref{thm:local-i-inputs}, and the formula for the Lelong number of a maximum, show that $b\sim_{\mathcal I}\varphi$: the Lelong numbers of $a-C$ on every local modification are at least those of $\varphi$, while those of $q$ equal them. Hence $b$ is a competitor for $Q_\theta[\varphi]=q$. Consequently $a-C\leq b\leq q$. Taking regularized suprema proves $E\leq q+C$.
edits.new:
For each competitor $a$, the upper bound $\sup_Xa\leq C$ and \cref{prop:p-below-i,prop:i-envelope-operations} give
\[
 a-C\leq a-\sup_Xa\leq Q_\theta[a]
                    \leq Q_\theta[\varphi]=q.
\]
Taking regularized suprema proves $E\leq q+C$.
